label: Dry spell broken by a sharp burst
description: One short rain episode arrives after a long preceding dry run.
window_note: The story is the break, not the total.
why_useful: Totals alone are misleading; the key is the sudden break after dryness.

label: Sustained wet stretch
description: Rain is distributed across many days, not concentrated in one spike.
window_note: A longer window is needed so the persistence is visible.
why_useful: This teaches the model to recognise persistence rather than a single heavy day.
key_facts: Window length: 30 days | Rain: 361.0mm vs normal 132.6mm | Rainy days: 30 | Wet streak in window: 30 days | Cool-day streak: 4 days

label: Rain concentrated into one short spell
description: A period looks wet on total rainfall, but nearly all of it comes from one brief burst.
window_note: Shorter framing prevents one burst from being misread as a wet fortnight.
why_useful: This teaches the model not to call a window broadly wet when the rain is concentrated.
key_facts: Window length: 7 days | Rain: 110.7mm vs normal 24.5mm | Rainy days: 3

label: Persistently dry window
description: Dryness itself is the main signal, relative to what is normal for the season.
window_note: A wider window is useful because absence is cumulative.
why_useful: This teaches the model to treat absence of rain as a real signal.
key_facts: Window length: 14 days | Rain: 1.1mm vs normal 57.7mm | Rainy days: 1 | Dry streak in window: 13 days | Hot-day streak: 13 days | Record days: 9

label: Daytime heat spell
description: High temperatures sit well above normal for several consecutive days.
window_note: The run-length matters more than any single hottest day.
why_useful: This teaches the model to prioritise a clear daytime heat run.

label: Warm-night run
description: Night temperatures stay unusually elevated even if daytime highs are not extreme.
window_note: This needs enough days for the night pattern to be unmistakable.
why_useful: This teaches the model not to miss elevated night temperatures when highs are less dramatic.

label: Cool daytime spell
description: Highs run meaningfully below normal for a sustained stretch.
window_note: This is about persistent daytime coolness, not a one-day dip.
why_useful: This teaches the model to spot sustained cool highs relative to normal.
key_facts: Window length: 14 days | Rain: 129.5mm vs normal 8.6mm | Rainy days: 14 | Wet streak in window: 14 days | Cool-day streak: 14 days

label: Cool-night run
description: Night temperatures stay below normal for several days.
window_note: The window is chosen to preserve the night-time pattern.
why_useful: This teaches the model to separate cool nights from cool days.
key_facts: Window length: 14 days | Rain: 1.8mm vs normal 54.7mm | Rainy days: 1 | Dry streak in window: 13 days | Cool-night streak: 14 days | Record days: 9

label: Record-heavy patch
description: Several days in the window broke prior calendar-date records.
window_note: The record cluster is the editorial hook.
why_useful: This teaches the model to foreground records when they cluster.

label: Wet month building through accumulation
description: The signal is cumulative rainfall excess over a month, not one isolated day.
window_note: A 30-day view is needed because the anomaly accumulates.
why_useful: This teaches the model that some stories are cumulative and need a month-long frame.

label: Dry month building through accumulation
description: The signal is a running monthly rainfall shortfall.
window_note: A 30-day view is needed because the deficit builds gradually.
why_useful: This teaches the model that rainfall deficits often need a month-long frame.

label: Heat-to-rain whiplash
description: The same window contains meaningful heat and then a clear rain break.
window_note: The chosen span keeps both parts of the story visible.
why_useful: This teaches the model to keep two linked signals in view instead of flattening them.
